settings.description: Title of the server in the browser lists; a short, unique name helps players find it again.
Text shown beneath the title in the in-game server list; an escape sequence is needed for a line break.
Whether the in-game public list advertises this server; the Steam browser listing is handled separately.
Primary UDP port players connect to. Needs a restart plus matching firewall and forwarding rules.
Second UDP port for direct client traffic. Must differ from the primary port; there is no launch flag for it.
Upper limit of connected non-admin players. Large counts strain map streaming; test before going past 32.
Join password every client must enter; blank means anyone can connect. Stored as plain text in the file.
Latency above which a player is disconnected; zero turns the check off.
Asks a UPnP-capable router to open the game ports by itself; turn off where forwarding is set up by hand.
Turns on Valve anti-cheat checks for joining Steam clients; a launch flag can override it.
Refuses new logins while the server reports an overload, protecting sessions already in progress.
TCP port of the remote console the Dialwarden hooks use. It only listens when the console password is set.
Shared secret for the remote console. Left empty, the console is silently off and no hook can reach the server.
On: a first-time player creates an account just by joining. Off: only accounts made by an admin can log in.
Build 41 only: it added unknown names to the whitelist. Build 42 ignores it; kept untouched when found, never added.
Deletes an account once its character dies, giving closed servers a one-life-per-account rule.
How many user names one Steam account may register on this server; zero removes the cap.
Rejects clients whose scripts differ from the server copy. Switch off only briefly while debugging mod mismatches.
Build 41 anti-cheat switch; Build 42 replaced the numbered switches with named integer settings. Kept, never added.
Mod IDs to activate, separated by semicolons, in load order. IDs may contain spaces; one Workshop item can hold several.
Numeric Workshop item IDs fetched when the server starts, separated by semicolons. Downloading an item does not activate the mods inside it.
Map folder names separated by semicolons. Custom maps come first; the base map entry is expected last.
Fixed x,y,z start location for every new character; 0,0,0 keeps the normal spawn region choice.
Item type IDs in Module.Item form, comma separated, given to each new character on first spawn.
World generation seed. Only takes effect on a fresh world or after the stored world-generation data is removed.
Soft-reset marker. A mismatch forces players to make new characters, so treat it as read-only unless wiping.
Master switch letting characters damage one another; the personal opt-in is handled by the safety system.
Gives each player a personal PVP toggle. With it off and PVP on, every player is always attackable.
Draws a marker above characters whose PVP toggle is active, so others can see who is hostile.
Delay before a change of a player's personal PVP state actually takes hold.
Scales close-combat damage between players; the stock value is far below full strength.
Scales gun damage between players; raise it for harsher encounters, lower it for softer ones.
Stops the in-game clock while nobody is online, so the world does not decay between sessions.
Lets tired characters use beds. Sleep stays optional unless needing sleep is also on.
Makes fatigue build up until characters must sleep. Has no effect while beds are not allowed.
How much faster game time runs while every connected player is asleep at once.
Blocks all fire except campfires, a common guard against arson griefing on public servers.
Broadcasts a chat notice to everyone whenever a player character dies.
Lets players knock each other to the ground. Experimental in Build 42 and may desync positions.
Caps the number of items per container, where every single nail counts; zero means no cap.
Scales how far running engines pull zombies in; lower values can also ease server load.
Permits demolishing walls and world objects with a sledgehammer; turn off to curb griefing.
Running into another player can shove them over; usually left off on crowded servers.
Age at which old blood decals are cleared when a chunk loads; zero keeps them. The sandbox file holds a copy of this key.
Allows ordinary players, not just staff, to claim a building as their protected safehouse.
Restricts safehouse claims to staff accounts; use it for curated or event servers.
Non-members may walk into a claimed safehouse. The key is misspelled by the game itself; never correct it.
Fire can damage claimed safehouses; turning it off protects them from arson.
Non-members may take items from containers inside a safehouse claimed by somebody else.
A member who dies can choose to come back inside the safehouse they belonged to.
In-game days a character must stay alive before being allowed to claim a safehouse.
Real-world hours of absence after which a member is removed from their safehouse.
Protection applies only while the owner is offline. Build 42 name; Build 41 used DisableSafehouseWhenPlayerConnected.
Containers inside claimed safehouses are skipped when the sandbox loot refill runs.
Lets players found factions with group tags; turn off for purely cooperative servers.
Enables the chat channel that reaches every connected player regardless of distance.
Comma list of chat channel codes clients may use: say, radio, admin, whisper, yell, safehouse, faction or all.
Greeting shown in chat at login. The game's own line-break and colour tags work inside it.
Shows the account name of each player floating above their character.
Names appear only while the cursor hovers over a character, which keeps the screen less cluttered.
Who shows up on the world map for each player.
Turns the built-in proximity voice chat on; its distance settings sit next to it in the file.
Shortest tile distance over which the built-in voice chat can be heard.
Longest tile distance over which the built-in voice chat can be heard.
Real-time interval for saving loaded map areas; zero relies only on the usual save moments.
How many rotating world backups the server keeps before deleting the oldest.
Takes a backup on every boot. Only checked at startup, so a change applies from the next start.
Gap between automatic backups while running; zero turns periodic backups off.
Connects global chat to a Discord channel through a bot account that you supply.
Bot token used by the Discord bridge. Treat it like a password and never show it in logs.
Build 42 channel name for relayed chat. Build 41 used a channel name and a channel id pair instead.
Population preset; choosing one also rewrites the population multiplier below it.
Where the dead gather across the map.
Respawn preset for the undead population.
Lets the horde drift into cleared cells over time.
Real duration of one game day.
Calendar month of the first day of a new world.
Clock time at world start.
Months already passed since the outbreak, which ages a new world.
When the taps run dry.
When the power grid fails.
Spawn weight for perishable food. A Build 42 number that replaces the Build 41 rarity scale.
Spawn weight for melee weapons that are not counted as tools.
Spawn weight for guns and their attachments.
Spawn weight for rounds, boxes and magazines.
Spawn weight for medicine and first-aid supplies.
Spawn weight for books that boost skill experience.
Catch-all weight for items without a category; it also affects foraging in towns.
Multiplies loot-table rolls. The game allows far more, but high values hurt performance, so this cap is lower.
Comma list of item types that never spawn as ordinary loot.
Game hours after which looted town containers refill; zero turns refills off.
Containers holding at least this many items are skipped by the refill.
Top chance in percent that a building is found already looted.
Climate offset for the whole map.
How often it rains across the world.
How fast nature reclaims the map.
Drain rate of hunger, thirst and fatigue.
How much foraging yields in the wild.
Spoilage pace of food.
When on, calories and nutrients change body weight and health.
New characters start with a small bag of basic gear.
Bonus or penalty trait points available at character creation.
Game hours before bodies vanish; zero also stops maggots.
How often the helicopter event happens.
Off-screen noises that pull zombies toward players.
How rare generators are.
Chance of tripping a house alarm.
How often house doors are locked.
Game hours before listed floor items are cleaned up; zero means off.
Sandbox copy of the blood decal lifetime; the ini file holds a key with the same name, and each file keeps its own.
Master switch for cars spawning in the world.
How many vehicles stand around the map.
Fuel left in found cars.
How often cars are locked.
Fuel pumps never run dry.
How often farms still hold livestock.
Peak vermin intensity in infested buildings.
How often random basements are placed.
Offers a corner minimap to players.
Experience rate for all skills, replacing the Build 41 global multiplier. The game allows far more; this cap keeps it sane.
On: the global rate applies to every skill. Off: the per-skill rates apply.
How fast zombies move once they notice prey.
Share of sprinters in percent, used only when movement is set to random.
How hard zombies hit.
How much damage zombies take before dying.
How the infection spreads.
Time until the infection kills.
Time until the infected dead rise again.
How clever zombies are.
How long zombies keep chasing.
How well zombies see.
How well zombies hear.
When the dead are fully active.
Zombies can break structures built by players.
Corpses that only pretend to be dead.
Crowd size needed to damage tall fences.
Base population factor written by the population preset; editing it directly overrides the preset.
Target zombie density on day one.
Target zombie density on the peak day.
Day on which the population target reaches its peak.
Game hours before a cell may repopulate; zero means never.
A chunk must go unobserved this long before it repopulates.
Share of the target population restored per respawn cycle.
Number of tracked zombies before cleanup starts. The game allows 0 to 5000; extreme values risk severe lag.
Build 41 global experience rate, replaced by the per-skill rates in Build 42. Kept, never added.
Build 41 rarity scale for food; Build 42 uses numeric spawn weights instead. Kept, never added.
Build 41 loot refill period, replaced by the hour-based refill in Build 42. Kept, never added.

rules.message: The remote console has no password, so it stays off and the save, announce and reload hooks cannot reach the server.
Two services share a port. The two game ports and the remote console port must all differ.
Workshop items are downloaded but no mod ID is activated, so none of them run.
Mods are activated with no Workshop items listed; fine for local mods, otherwise they will not load.
The server is closed, so an admin must create every account; automatic whitelisting no longer exists in Build 42.
Sleep is required but beds are not allowed, so the need for sleep is ignored.
The sprinter share only applies when zombie movement is set to random.
The server is listed publicly, open to new accounts and has no join password.
A Build 41 key in a Build 42 file: the automatic whitelist no longer exists in Build 42. The game ignores it and it is kept untouched.
A Build 41 key in a Build 42 file: Build 42 replaced the numbered anti-cheat switches. The game ignores it and it is kept untouched.
A Build 41 key in a Build 42 file: Build 42 reads the per-skill rates instead. The game ignores it and it is kept untouched.
A Build 41 key in a Build 42 file: Build 42 reads the numeric spawn weights. The game ignores it and it is kept untouched.
A Build 41 key in a Build 42 file: Build 42 reads the hour-based refill. The game ignores it and it is kept untouched.

presets.label: Apocalypse (42 defaults)
presets.description: The values a freshly generated Build 42 server writes: normal population, no respawns, utilities failing early.

presets.label: Builder
presets.description: Peaceful building: no PVP, no fire, fewer zombies, utilities that stay on and faster skill growth.

presets.label: Survivor, hard
presets.description: Scarce loot, sprinters mixed in, fast corpse removal and rare loot refills for a harsh run.
